description: The requests of ./bench.sh smoke. Every entry is a GET, except one POST that the search route rejects before it searches. An entry with 'directRoles' is skipped when the requests go straight to a process in another role (--host): through the public route, the proxy sends it to a search role. 'guards' says which regression or edge the entry is for. Titles and people are public catalog entries. Never add a user's handle or list: the share list comes from config.env.

static.guards: The static hostname serves the deployed build with CORS and CDN cache headers, and never serves the home page.

entries.guards: The landing page renders, and it references the static asset that a later entry requests.
A full movie page: the title, related title links in the server HTML, images from the image host, and JSON-LD.
A full show page, with seasons and episode scores.
1e459198: a title without a poster answered 500, because the image helper called replace() on a null path.
1e459198, the other null path: a title with a poster and no backdrop. Also a show with more than 1,000 cast links.
A title with no cast rows and no related titles: empty lists must render, not crash.
A title without any video: the trailer section has nothing to show.
A title without streaming data in any country.
Grey's Anatomy has more than 3,300 cast rows: the largest page render, and the first to time out or run out of memory.
A full person page.
Fixed in 0c0825ec: 6,603 people without a department answered 500, because the meta text called toLowerCase() on null.
The gate for the endless filtered person URLs: a browser without the cookie gets the small check page, which no cache may store.
90aa853c: with the cookie, the filtered person page itself answers.
A crawler that names itself is sent to the unfiltered person page.
Discover renders its first rows on the server. It needs the title snapshot, so it is empty right after a failed snapshot load.
Discover with a filter in the URL.

The share list page, the primary viral scenario. An anonymous request for a public list gets the keyed policy, so the page cache may store it: private, no-store here means every request renders again. The path comes from config.env and is never printed.
The share list's link preview image, as a link-preview bot requests it. da485db3 also fixed how the share card renderer finds its file.
A share list that doesn't exist answers 404, not 500 and not 200.
A title that doesn't exist answers 404, not 500 and not 200.
A title's link preview image, read from the cache cluster as a buffer or rendered in a child process. A generic busy answer has a lifetime of 60 seconds and no ETag, and fails here.
Links shared before October 4, 2026 name the .png URL. It answers with the same JPEG.
The public directory is in the image, and crawlers get their rules. Title pages link to filtered Discover URLs, which crawlers must not follow.
A path that no route names answers 404. A redirect to the start page reads as a soft 404 to a crawler.
An unknown category under a known type answers 404, not a redirect to the type's hub.
An unknown page of a known category answers 404.
A hub without structured data has no JSON-LD block, not an empty one. It also shows that the 404 for unknown paths didn't take the hubs with it.
The second page of a category page lists other titles, so its canonical address names the page and not the first one.
The old address of the shows hub moves for good, not to the start page.
An old shows address keeps the rest of its path and its query. The fixed-depth routes must win over the category routes.
An old explore address with a category page of the same name moves to that page, not to a hub.
An old explore address without a page that replaces it answers 404.
The sitemap that robots.txt names is served as a file. The answer for removed sitemap files must not take it.
A sitemap file that was removed answers 410, not a redirect to the start page.
631ae6c4 moved build files: a script that the home page's HTML references must exist, with a one-year cache lifetime.
The metrics are on a private port only. The public port must not serve them.
A related titles panel other than the default one. The page requests it when a visitor selects a panel, so no server render covers it.
Every page requests the search configuration after it loads.
The header search: it reads the search index and the people index in memory, and sends no model call. With search roles, the proxy sends this path to them.

The search route answers from a process that runs search. One character of text is rejected after the in-flight limit and before the search starts (routes/api.combined-search.ts), so nothing is read, paid for, or written: a search that runs writes a history row. A 503 here means that the request reached a page role, that no search role is ready, or that four searches were in flight.

The home page's pool for a country without a key in the streaming order answered 503 (ColumnUnknownException). The page sends it as a POST with the guest's progress: the GET reads the same pool for a guest without progress.
